sentences.text: Ms. Alotriya Mukherjee  For the Petitioner Mr. Sourav Chatterjee  For the State
Heard the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the parties.
Perused the Case Diary.

It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the prosecution has launched the criminal proceeding under sections 272/273/420/120B of the Indian Penal Code when In Re: Prosenjit Ghosh vs The State Of West Bengal on 12 October, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/74694269/

sentences.text: there is a Special Act being the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

It is further submitted that there is a special procedure provided for investigation in relation to an offence committed under the Special Act and in view of the judgment rendered by the Supreme Court in the case of Jeewan Kumar Raut & Another - Vs- Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in (2009) 7 Supreme Court Cases 526, the charging sections under the Indian Penal Code is impliedly overruled and/or superseded by the provisions  2 of the Special Act.

entities.text: Jeewan Kumar Raut & Another - Vs- Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in (2009) 7 Supreme Court Cases 526
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We do not find that the aforesaid judgment can lend any support to the petitioner in the given facts and circumstances of the instant case.
In the said report, the case was registered on the offence committed under section 22 of the Transplantation of Human Organs Act, 1994 and under the different provisions of the Indian Penal Code.

In the backdrop of the aforesaid perspective, it wa held that once the Special Act provides the procedural mechanism for investigation, the investigation under the general processual law cannot continue.

It would be apt to quote the observation recorded in paragraph 26 of the said judgment, which runs thus :
 "It is a well-settled principle of law that if a special statute lays down  procedures, the ones laid down under the general statutes shall not be  followed.
In a situation of this nature, the respondent could carry out investigation in exercise of its authorisation under Section 13(3)(iv) of TOHO.
While doing so, it could exercise such powers which are otherwise vested in it.
But, as it could not file a police report but a complaint petition only; sub-section (2) of Section 167 of the Code may not be applicable".
In the instant case, the case has been registered under the aforementioned sections of the Indian Penal Code and none of the sections of the Special Act has been invoked and/or set in motion.
This Court, therefore, does not find that the petitioner has been able to make out a good case for grant of bail.

Apart from the same, taking into account the quantity of material seized from the custody of the petitioner and the gravity of the offence committed by him, we do not feel that this is a fit case where the petitioner should be released on bail.
The application for bail being C.R.M. 9726 of 2017 is, thus, rejected.

(Harish Tandon, J.) (Md. Mumtaz Khan, J.)
